title: Evolution Of The Layered Structure Of Earth
definition: The geological and chemical process through which the homogeneous primordial Earth differentiated into distinct concentric zones—crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core—primarily driven by planetary heating and gravitational segregation.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding geodynamics, plate tectonics, internal heat sources, and earthquake wave propagation, frequently tested in Prelims (direct statements on density stratification and seismic discontinuities) and Mains GS-1 (Geomorphology).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Evolution Of The Layered Structure Of Earth.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Origin of the Earth and Solar System
Basic Physics of Gravity and Heat Transfer
